pol_micro_heading_deviation → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment intra_scale Deviation from the global school heading makes a fish more likely to be misaligned with its local contact neighbors as well.

pol_micro_heading_deviation → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward A deviant fish can influence neighbors through social alignment, but since alignment pulls toward the group, the net effect may be to increase local heterogeneity, raising component mean deviation.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment upward When individual fish align with their contact neighbors, a locally shared escape heading can spread across the component; this social alignment can turn component mean heading toward the away-from-shark direction.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Fish closer to a shark experience stronger threat and may align their headings with nearby escaping fish, increasing polarization within their contact component.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment upward High shark proximity for component members can bias component mean heading away from the nearest shark, raising meso away-from-shark alignment.
pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_macro_school_polarization upward If many fish are simultaneously close to sharks, their shared escape alignment can raise whole-school heading polarization.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov upward Individual proximity responses contribute to how school polarization varies with mean proximity across time, making micro proximity a plausible input to the run-level macro covariance.
pol_meso_component_polarization → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment intra_scale A polarized component heading can align with the away-from-shark direction under escape bias.
pol_meso_component_polarization → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Heading alignment within contact components contributes to the global alignment of fish headings.
pol_meso_component_polarization → pol_macro_polarization_change upward Step changes in component polarization can drive changes in whole-school polarization.
pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_micro_heading_deviation downward A polarized collective heading can constrain individual headings, plausibly reducing focal deviation from the school mean.

pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward School-level polarization implies more similar headings across neighbors, plausibly increasing a focal fish's alignment with its contact neighbors.
pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_meso_component_polarization downward A highly polarized school provides a strong common heading field that can raise polarization within contact components.

pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward When school-wide polarization is high, component headings are plausibly drawn toward the common direction, reducing mean component heading deviation.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → pol_meso_component_polarization downward The run-level polarization-proximity coupling sets how much local components align during threat, so component-level polarization can vary with this global coupling regime.
pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → pol_macro_school_polarization intra_scale Runs where polarization tracks shark proximity can exhibit higher polarization during threat periods.
pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → pol_macro_polarization_change intra_scale Threat-coupled polarization indicates responsiveness to shark proximity, affecting step changes in polarization.

pol_macro_polarization_change → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward An increase in whole-school heading polarization reflects stronger collective alignment, which can propagate into components and reduce the mean angular deviation of component headings.

Indicator=(1/|C|) sum_{i in C} |atan2(sin(theta_i-Theta_C), cos(theta_i-Theta_C))|. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

Let s* be the nearest shark to c_C and a=(c_C-p_s*)/||c_C-p_s*||. Indicator=cos(Theta_C)·a_x+sin(Theta_C)·a_y. Indicator=(1/T) sum_t (R(t)-mean R)(q(t)-mean q) over steps with both defined. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}
